idiom_name: lazy val (virtual proxy) + explicit forwarding / export clause / Dynamic
implementation_notes: Scala's virtual proxy is a keyword: `lazy val` defers evaluation to first access and memoizes the result, with the runtime handling the initialization race. For the interposition kind, a class or trait holds the subject and forwards explicitly; Scala 3's export clause can generate the forwarding members for you (`export real.{draw as _, *}` forwards everything except the operations you override), while scala.Dynamic with selectDynamic/applyDynamic handles unknown members as a runtime-checked dynamic proxy. The stdlib's scala.Proxy trait forwards only equals/hashCode/toString to a self object and is rarely what is wanted; there is no class-delegation keyword as in Kotlin, so export or an explicit wrapper is the idiomatic replacement.
code_sketch:
class ImageProxy(real: Image) extends Image:
  export real.{draw as _, *}                     // generated forwarding, draw excluded
  override def draw(id: String): Bitmap =
    cache.getOrElseUpdate(id, real.draw(id))

object Document:
  lazy val image: Image = HeavyImage("big.png")  // virtual proxy
pitfalls: A lazy val holds a lock while its initializer runs; blocking work inside it serializes first access, and a self-referential lazy val either loops or deadlocks.
Dynamic calls are checked only at runtime - typos in member names compile and fail later - so prefer explicit forwarding or export when type safety matters.
export generates final aliases; a member you also want to override must be excluded with `x as _` or the override will not compile.
